lines.text: Gus has to eat a burger every three minutes, and that's not even his biggest problem.
At seven this morning he woke up with the metabolism of a hummingbird.
Gram for gram, that tiny bird burns fuel fifty times as fast as he does.
At his size, that's a hundred and twenty thousand calories a day.
His wife flips pancakes as fast as she can. Gone.
His neighbor laughs that no one eats that much and loses every sausage on the grill.
His heart beats twenty times a second. That's not a pulse, that's a hum.
But wait. Why is his helmet steaming up?
You see, all that food turns into heat, and Gus now puts out as much as four space heaters.
Ever notice a french fry goes cold in minutes, but a baked potato stays hot for half an hour?
Small things have more skin for their size. Pound for pound, the bird has twenty times more than Gus, so its heat just leaks away.
Gus is the baked potato. He heats up more than a degree every minute.
Luckily, he lives by the sea, and water pulls heat out far faster than air.
Unluckily, it's now been four minutes since he last ate.
And the funny part? Even a hummingbird can't afford to live like one.
On cold nights it almost shuts off, just to make it to breakfast.
